paragraphs: R' Shimon Shezuri: Mishnah Demai 4:1; Shevi'it 2:8; Gittin 6:5; Hullin 4:5; Keritut 4:3; Kelim 18:1; Tohorot 3:2; Tevul Yom 4:5. He was called Shezuri after his occupation, as Rambam writes. It seems to me that there is a place in Upper Galilee called Shezur, and he is buried there, as I saw in writings sent from the Land of Israel about the burial places of the righteous. So too I saw in גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael]; see R' Yishmael ben Elisha the high priest. Heilprin reports a reading in Merubbeh in which R' Shimon Shezuri describes his father's household as among the householders of Upper Galilee. The compared Bavli reads R' Yishmael, and the Tosefta reads R' Yishmael Shezuri. In Sifra and Jerusalem Ha-Matznia, halakhah 4 (where Heilprin proposes a scribal error because of the parallel in Keritut), we find R' Yishmael Shezuri; see his entry. Perhaps he was his brother, or someone else from there. In Mishnah Keritut 4:3, 19a, R' Shimon Shezuri and R' Shimon say, and likewise R' Yehudah. Thus we find him a colleague of R' Meir, R' Yehudah, R' Shimon, and R' Yose in Kelim, chapter 18. But in Rosh Hashanah, first chapter, 13b, and Menahot 30b, R' Yose ben Kippur reports in R' Shimon Shezuri's name, which suggests that he was earlier, since R' Yose ben Kippur lived in the time of R' Hananyah, R' Yehoshua's nephew. In Tosefta Demai, chapter 4 as cited (5:24 in the compared text), and Jerusalem Demai, end of chapter 5, he asked R' Tarfon. Likewise in Menahot 31a, he asked R' Tarfon about untithed produce that became mixed with his unconsecrated produce. Abba Hanan in R' Eliezer's name … R' Shimon Shezuri says … he said to him …: Nazir 45a. R' Hanina said, “The halakhah follows R' Shimon Shezuri. Moreover, wherever R' Shimon Shezuri taught, the halakhah follows him”: Menahot 30b. There R' Yehudah, R' Yose, R' Yitzhak, and R' Shimon Shezuri disagree; see Tosafot there and Hullin 75b. Also Shakh, Yoreh De'ah, no. 276, subparagraph 7, and responsa Bah.
